experiment: audit prompt section order: page-before-statement (cacheable) vs statement-before-page (current)
design: A1/A2 = current prompt twice (control for judge self-noise); B = reordered prompt. Same (claim,url,page) triples throughout.
reading: the judge disagrees with itself on 0 of 30, and with the reordered prompt on 6 of 30, so the shift is attributable to the reorder rather than to noise. Net effect on headline citation accuracy: 77.8% -> 84.6%.
decision: reorder rejected; prompt caching refused. See docs/adr/0003-no-prompt-caching.md
limits: n=30 on one question. Detects a shift of roughly this size; a smaller systematic drift would not clear this sample.
